svg.title: Thesium Codex — 3. Holding agents to it, and measuring the gaps
svg.desc: On plan and implement, a gate refuses work done without a configured consultation. A per-run ledger classifies every miss by the first rung that leaked.
svg.text: Thesium Codex — 3. Holding agents to it, and measuring the gaps
On plan and implement, a gate refuses work done without a configured consultation. A per-run ledger classifies every miss by the first rung that leaked.
GATE · :codex-consultation (§7.4.3) · plan, implement
Off, or no situation: pass clean
Status unconfigured or unmapped. A gate that nags about an optional
capability trains people to ignore gates. Governance set: a workflow
override cannot drop it.
Configured but skipped: FAIL
The operator asked for codex governance, and the phase ran without it.
That is a silent downgrade, so the gate fails closed: :codex-
consultation-skipped.
Pinned, never fetched: pass + warning
:codex-pin-not-fetched. With the body inlined, the agent saw it
anyway. When the planner sheds bodies to a manifest (N12 §6), it means
the landings were never seen, and the gate still only warns.
Warnings are kept
A warning never changes the decision, so the decision envelope cannot
carry it. The phase result keeps it as :phase/gate-warnings, and the
append-only gate-history.edn records it on every iteration, so it
survives a redirect or repair that overwrites the checkpoint.
GAP LEDGER · written at phase leave
Miss signals
Blocking review issues, gate failures (namespaced :phase/gate-errors)
and terminal anomalies visible when the phase leaves.
First leak wins
uncovered: no situation for the phase; the codex never entered.
misrouted: the problem was identified, but is not reachable from the
entered board.
undelivered: routed, but the consultation was skipped or absent, or
the codex was unconfigured.
unheeded: the warning was in front of the agent and the failure
matched a delivered landing anyway.
A miss below the attribution threshold, or whose landings cannot be
read, goes to the review queue: in no bucket, but counted as open
learning.
Files, per run
Under <checkpoint-root>/<run-id>/:
codex-gap-ledger.edn: one miss per line
codex-consultations.edn: one consultation per consulting leave
gate-history.edn: every gate decision
All three are append-only. The two codex files are opt-in (nothing is
written without MINIFORGE_CODEX_PATH); gate history is written for
every gated run.
READ-OUTS · bb tasks
bb codex-gap-report
The T2 §4 gap vector over run ledgers: coverage, routing, anchoring,
delivery (with pin-read counts), attention, learning and the review queue,
each slot listing its member miss ids.
bb codex-gap-peg-telemetry
§7.7 per-peg telemetry. The mapped mechanism's gate verdict counts first;
without one, explicit answer_peg answers count; with neither, nothing is
invented. A verdict that outranks an answer is reported as a disagreement.
Entropy near zero means a retirement candidate (§4.4.1); identical branch
landings mean the board collapsed and needs a merge.
bb codex-gap-retrodict
T2 §5.4: re-classify recorded misses against the codex as it is now,
keeping the recorded bucket beside the new one. It is pure over data, so
no workflow re-runs. This is the evidence a new peg needs before promotion
feeds promotion: panel 4
